newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong dollar, money market sighs in relief.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong dollar, money market sighs in relief.

text.p: * Hong Kong dollar settles back after rates shot up on Thursday, trading steadily in a range
* Dealers said the mood quite different on Friday, calm and the market not particularly active
* But tension lingers with head currency traders cautioning that speculators are still circling the region. Fear of another round of attack on regional currencies still prevalent
* "Some people felt the Hong Kong dollar was not immune," one trader said. "But the extraordinarily high interest rate helped to keep the Hong Kong dollar stable."
* Currency forwards still wide but signficantly more relaxed than on Thursday
* Hong Kong Monetary Authority released Exchange Fund reserve figures after market close in a "clear bid to tell the speculators not to even think about it," one analyst said
* HKMA, Hong Kong's de facto central bank, said it held HK$569 billion in the Exchange Fund at June 30, up 6.4 percent from December 31, 1996.
* Official foreign exchange reserves, including those held in the Land Fund, exceeded US$82 billion at June 30
* "Whether the HKMA intervened or not, they're letting the rate squeeze up and when they released their reserves - well, it was a clear warning," the analyst said
* Lower yields on Hong Kong paper narrowed spreads against corresponding U.S. treasuries
* Traders focussed on meeting of regional central bankers in Shanghai
* Yields on Exchange Fund Notes: 3yr 6.67 percent; 5yr 6.78 percent; 7yr 6.87 percent; one week 6.34 percent.
